title: Retroactive Medicaid Eligibility and Rebillable Charges — Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility
content:
**Desk guidance.** When an Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility record of the Medicaid Fee-for-Service class is added with an effective date earlier than the date it is added, charges on the patient's other coverage accounts become rebillable to Medicaid when their originating line's date of service falls:

- on or after that effective date, and
- no more than the class's retroactive-eligibility period (in calendar days) before the date the record is added.

Each such open charge is removed in full with the reason "retro Medicaid rebill", and any patient payment already applied to such a charge is refunded under the credit refund rule once the adjustment leaves a credit. Charges outside that window stay with the patient.

## Window illustration (hypothetical dates; period taken as 90 days)

Medicaid record added on 1 October with an effective date of 1 June. Ninety calendar days before 1 October is 3 July.

| Originating line's date of service | On or after 1 June? | No more than 90 days before 1 October? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 May | no | — | stays with the patient |
| 20 June | yes | no (more than 90 days before) | stays with the patient |
| 3 July | yes | yes (exactly 90 days) | open charge removed in full as retro Medicaid rebill |
| 15 August | yes | yes | open charge removed in full as retro Medicaid rebill |

## Point of judgement

A charge in the window that the patient already paid in part is still removed in full by the retro Medicaid rebill adjustment; the patient payment already applied to it is refunded under the credit refund rule once that adjustment leaves a credit.
